name: EUV lithography (ASML monopoly)
description_md: Every leading-edge logic wafer (TSMC N3/N2, Intel 18A/14A, Samsung SF2) and increasingly leading-edge DRAM requires extreme-ultraviolet lithography, and exactly one company on earth — ASML — can build the machines. Scanner lead times run a year or more, ASML entered 2026 with a record ~€38.8B backlog, and each fab expansion anywhere in the chain (N2 capacity, HBM4 DRAM lines, US fabs) queues behind ASML tool slots and Tokyo Electron's matching coater/developer tracks (~100% share). The next-generation High-NA ramp is real but early: the first production-grade EXE:5200B shipped Q4 2025, adoption is limited to Intel (14A), Samsung, and SK Hynix, and TSMC has said it will not use High-NA in volume production before ~2029 on cost (>€350M/tool) grounds. Status basis: judged binding because a single supplier with >12-month lead times and record backlog gates the pace at which every downstream compute constraint (foundry, HBM, packaging) can be expanded — even though EUV tool supply is not the most acutely rationed input in 2026.

controlled_by.share_note: 100% of EUV/High-NA scanner supply (structural monopoly; disclosed)
~100% of EUV coater/developer tracks paired with ASML scanners (company_claimed)

dependents.dependency_md: All N5/N3/N2 capacity — >90% of leading-edge foundry output — is printed on ASML EUV; N2 expansion (~90-100k wpm by early 2026) is paced by scanner deliveries.
18A ramp and 14A (first High-NA node, target 2027) depend on EUV and EXE:5200 deliveries; Intel is ASML's lead High-NA customer.
SF2 GAA logic and leading-edge DRAM/HBM4 base-die work require EUV; a High-NA early adopter.
1c-nm-class DRAM for HBM4 uses EUV layers; capacity adds queue for the same scanners as logic.
Indirect but total: every Blackwell/Rubin die exists only because an ASML scanner printed it; no substitute path exists at any price.

substitutes_md: None at leading edge. DUV multi-patterning can in principle substitute at old nodes (as SMIC does at 7nm-class in China under export controls) but with severe yield/cost penalties and it cannot reach N3/N2-class density economically. Nikon/Canon exited the leading-edge scanner race years ago; no second source is plausible inside a decade. The only 'substitute' is time — waiting for ASML capacity.
downcycle_md: ASML is among the best-protected names in the chain in a downturn: tools are ordered years ahead with deposits, the backlog is diversified beyond AI (mobile, auto, memory), and litho capacity is the last thing a fab cancels because it is the longest to re-acquire. In 2001- and 2019-style semi downcycles ASML saw order pushouts rather than mass cancellations. The glut would form downstream (idle fab capacity, falling wafer prices at TSMC/Samsung) before ASML's P&L took the hit; the High-NA ramp would slow first since it is the discretionary, unproven capex item (TSMC has already deferred it).

observations.notes: Sole supplier of EUV and High-NA scanners worldwide.
Record backlog entering 2026; FY26 shipments skewed to 2H on customer cleanroom readiness.
At least ~12 months for EUV systems; High-NA effectively longer (install + qualification measured in years).
First production-grade EXE:5200B shipped for Intel 14A (2027 target); imec qualification unit targeted 4Q26; TSMC says no High-NA volume production before ~2029.
